holidays.name: National Cookie Day
holidays.description: A day devoted to the glory of cookies in all shapes, from chocolate chip to snickerdoodle. Bakeries and cookie fans mark it with giveaways, swaps, and tray after tray of warm treats.
holidays.origin: Founded by Cookie Cottage founder Ann Warner as a promotional observance in the 1980s and 90s. It lands in the middle of holiday baking season and grew into an annual tradition.
holidays.funFact: The word 'cookie' comes from the Dutch 'koekje,' meaning 'little cake.' Early cookies were test cakes: bakers dropped small bits of batter in the oven to check its temperature.

holidays.name: National Sock Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the humble sock, the unsung hero of cozy feet. People show off wild patterns, buy new pairs, and donate socks to those in need.
holidays.origin: An informal, pop-culture observance that spread through social media and sock brands, who encourage people to wear fun socks and to give pairs to shelters.
holidays.funFact: Socks are among the most requested items at homeless shelters, because they are rarely donated and wear out fast.

holidays.name: Wear Brown Shoes Day
holidays.description: A day for dusting off your brown footwear, and for pondering whether you've been wearing black shoes out of habit. It is a small but sincere salute to the earthy tones of the shoe world.
holidays.origin: A little-known unofficial observance of uncertain origin. It circulates through calendar lists of quirky days and is popular among shoe enthusiasts.
holidays.funFact: An old menswear rule says 'no brown in town,' meaning brown shoes were once considered too casual for formal city business.

holidays.name: International Day of Banks
holidays.description: A day recognizing banks, which keep money moving and give piggy banks a day of rest. It is also a good time to reflect on how and where we save.
holidays.origin: Listed on the United Nations-related calendars and in observance lists as a day to acknowledge the role of banking institutions. Its international status has made it a recurring entry in global observance calendars.
holidays.funFact: The word 'bank' comes from the Italian 'banca,' meaning bench, after the benches where medieval Italian money changers worked in the marketplace.

holidays.name: Santa's Workshop Day
holidays.description: A cheerful December day for imagining the North Pole at full production, with elves, toy builders, and sleigh repairs. Families and crafters get festive with DIY toy-making and workshop-themed fun.
holidays.origin: An informal seasonal observance growing out of Christmas folklore and pop culture, popularized in 19th-century American stories and poems about Santa's toy shop.
holidays.funFact: Early Santa illustrations by cartoonist Thomas Nast in the 1860s and 70s helped establish the idea of a North Pole workshop.
